title: V Cv 3 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: V Cv 3 cassava: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: V Cv 3 cassava is a cassava variety. About 12 months to harvest, 28.2 t/ha in trials. See its ratings and traits. Compare it with others.
excerpt: V Cv 3 is a registered cassava variety. The Philippine Seed Board approved it in 1990. It takes about 12 months from planting to harvest, with 28.25 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about V Cv 3 cassava
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

V Cv 3 cassava takes about 12 months from planting to harvest. That is 1.5 months longer than the average of the 42 cassava varieties with a day count, 10.5 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 28.25 t/ha trails the average of its group, 32.38. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit cassava fields most often: [whitefly](/pests/whitefly), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its roots have white flesh and brown skin. Dry matter is 31.1 percent. A higher dry matter cooks mealy and gives processors more flour or starch from each tonne. The starch content is 29.1 percent.
Where and when to plant V Cv 3 cassava

Pick by buyer first. Starch and feed plants pay for yield and starch content, while the table wants a sweet, low cyanide variety that boils soft. A high starch variety needs a buyer within a day of harvest, because the roots spoil fast.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 12 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 28.25 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of V Cv 3?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
